function: DNN model of the non-separable pixel-RIS response, used for cascaded channel estimation/prediction and discrete RIS state configuration maximizing sum rate (p. 1, p. 5, p. 12).
system: Downlink MU-MISO, BS 4x1 ULA (K=2) or 4x2 UPA (K=4); reflecting pixel-based RIS, 8x8 elements, 16 states; 2.4 GHz, 60 kHz (p. 6, p. 10, p. 11).
method: Supervised DNN (product-feature, attention, fully connected modules) fitting the RIS response (NMSE loss, Adam); model-based LS estimation; softmax-relaxed beamforming solved by Adam (p. 6, p. 8, p. 10).
data_channel: DNN: 10^7 training, 10^6 test random angle pairs per state of pixel-RIS response [4]; channels: 3GPP 38.901 Sec. 7.5 Indoor-Office, K-factor 3 dB (p. 6, p. 10).
test_conditions: DNN: held-out random angle pairs; system: 10x8 m femtocell, 100 random-location snapshots, 40 realizations, two setups, SNR 0-10 dB, NMSE on unseen RIS configurations (p. 6, p. 10, p. 11).
baselines: Random states, Best Sounding (best of 16 sounded states), Group-Opt [40],[41] and phased-array RIS with perfect CSI; DNN versus own kernel approximation; no learned baseline (p. 7, p. 11).
metrics: NMSE of RIS response approximation; NMSE of channel prediction on unseen RIS configurations; sum achievable rate versus SNR; FLOPs, parameters, memory (p. 6, p. 7, p. 11).
complexity: DNN: 1432 FLOPs, 550 parameters, 196 KB memory (Table II, p. 7); Algorithm 1 O(MI^3+MI^2BK+KJ^3+MBKJ^2) (p. 8); Algorithm 2 linear in |D| (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 10: "Channel coefficients are generated using the 3GPP ray-tracing model [37, Section 7.5] with parameters for the Indoor-Office scenario"; p. 13: "[37] Study on channel model for frequencies from 0.5 to 100 GHz. 3GPP TS 38.901".
q2_support: p. 6: "Likewise, the validation and testing sets consist of 10^6 samples each." The DNN is tested on held-out angle pairs of the same random draw; no other scenario, band, RIS, or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "we consider the following baselines: Random ... Best Sounding ... Group-Opt [40], [41] ... Phased Array", all non-learned; p. 7: the DNN is compared only with the paper's own "product-Legendre-kernel-based solution"; no earlier learned method.
q4_support: p. 7: "We show the complexity of our two proposed solutions in Table II, detailing the number of DNN parameters, FLOPs, and memory needed for storage" (DNN: 1432 FLOPs, 550 parameters).
q5_support: p. 10: "Channel coefficients are generated using the 3GPP ray-tracing model"; p. 6: "The training dataset is generated by randomly selecting" angle pairs. Simulated data only; no link to code or data, no public dataset.
notes: PDF is arXiv:2510.20354v1; its title and authors match the Crossref record of the DOI (IEEE Trans. Wireless Commun., 2026). Eligibility is borderline on check 3 (no_learning): the only learned component is a supervised DNN that approximates the pixel-RIS element response nu(phi_in, phi_out; l) (pp. 5-6). Channel estimation (LS and grid search, Algorithms 1-2, pp. 8-10) and passive beamforming (softmax relaxation optimized per instance with Adam, no training, p. 10) are model-based. I include it because the DNN output enters the regressors of the cascaded-channel estimator, the channel prediction for RIS states never sounded, and the beamforming objective (p. 12: "We introduced a DNN to model the RIS response function"). The reviewer should confirm that a learned model of the RIS response counts as a learned component that performs the function; if not, exclude as no_learning (p. 8, p. 10). Area: the solution addresses channel estimation (area 2) and passive beamforming (area 3) together. The main metric is the sum rate (p. 5: "The primary objective of this paper is to configure an appropriate RIS state st to maximize the sum rate"; Figs. 11-12 are the only comparisons with baselines), so area 3. Area 2 is the alternative if the DNN is read as channel synthesis. q1: the DNN is trained on samples of the RIS element response (the paper does not say whether these come from EM simulation or measurement of the prototype in [4]), not on channels. All channel-dependent evaluation uses 3GPP 38.901 Sec. 7.5, Indoor-Office (Table 7.5-6) with the K-factor set to 3 dB. The paper calls this the "3GPP ray-tracing model" and cites it as TS 38.901 v18.0.0; Sec. 7.5 is the fast-fading model of TR 38.901. The system model is also stated to follow "the 3GPP channel model [37, Section 7]" (p. 4). The paper does not say whether the DNN or the kernel approximation is used in the simulations of Figs. 10-12. q2: the channel-prediction NMSE uses "100 random RIS configurations not observed during the channel sounding phases" (p. 11). That tests the model-based estimator, not the trained DNN, and the DNN does not depend on M or K, so the two setups are not a new condition for it. q3: the channel-estimation NMSE (Fig. 10) has no baseline at all.
